items.title: lazy-fix
items.text:
Check and fix Python imports into PEP 810 lazy imports.

PEP 810 adds a lazy soft keyword to Python 3.15: lazy import json and lazy from pathlib import Path defer the actual import until the name is first used. lazy-fix is a CST-based (LibCST) tool that finds eligible module-level imports in your codebase and rewrites them to that syntax, so you don't have to do it by hand.

items.title: Install
items.text: uv add --dev lazy-fix

items.title: Quickstart
items.text:
lazy-fix check .
lazy-fix fix .

check reports imports that should be lazy but aren't, and exits with a non-zero status if it finds any — use it as a CI gate. fix rewrites them in place; pass --diff to preview the changes without writing.

items.title: Targeting pre-3.15 projects
items.text: If a project's requires-python doesn't allow 3.15 yet, lazy-fix falls back to PEP 810's own forward-compatibility mechanism: a __lazy_modules__ list declared under the imports, rather than the lazy import syntax itself. See PEP 810 and lazy_modules.

items.title: CLI reference
items.text:
lazy-fix check [path ...] [options]
lazy-fix fix [path ...] [options]

Each path is a file or a directory, and directories are recursed into. Only .py files are considered. Dot-prefixed directories/files and .gitignore-matched paths are skipped.

items.title: Project root
items.text:
With no path, lazy-fix scans the whole project from its root. It finds the root by walking up from the current directory. The first directory holding a lazy-fix.toml or a pyproject.toml is the root. With neither, the git root is used, and with no git repository, the current directory.

Configuration is always read from the project root, including when you pass explicit paths. Paths only limit what is scanned.

items.title: check
items.text: Reports non-lazy imports that should be lazy, per your configuration. Writes nothing. Exits 1 if any violations are found, 0 otherwise — suitable as a CI gate.

items.title: fix
items.text:
Rewrites eligible imports to lazy form and exits 0 once done.

Flag Description --diff / --dry-run Print the changes without writing them

items.title: Run your formatter afterwards
items.text: The output of fix is valid Python, but it is not formatted. lazy-fix leaves formatting to your own tools. A long __lazy_modules__ list can trip line length rules such as E501, and where the marker sits can trip import sorting rules such as I001, until a formatter runs. Run your formatter after fix, for example ruff format and ruff check --fix.

items.title: Exit codes
items.text: Command Exit code Meaning check 0 No violations found check 1 One or more non-lazy imports found fix 0 Fix ran (whether or not it changed anything) check, fix 2 The configuration is invalid, for example the same entry in allow and deny

items.title: Configuration reference
items.text:
Config lives in a [tool.lazy-fix] table. lazy-fix reads it from the project root, from lazy-fix.toml if that exists and from pyproject.toml otherwise. Both files use the same [tool.lazy-fix] table and keys. See CLI reference for how the root is found.

[tool.lazy-fix]
deny = ["sqlalchemy"]
allow = ["sqlalchemy.orm"]
exclude = ["build/", "migrations/"]

lazy-fix only reads these files. It never creates or rewrites them.

Breaking change in 0.2.0

Every module is now eligible by default, where before only modules listed in allow were. A lazy-fix.toml with top-level keys (allow = [...]) must move them under [tool.lazy-fix]. Top-level keys are ignored, and lazy-fix logs a warning when it finds them.

items.title: Options
items.text: Key Type Description deny list of module names Modules that are never made lazy allow list of module names Modules made lazy even when a broader deny entry covers them exclude list of glob patterns Files and directories to skip

items.title: Which modules are eligible
items.text:
Every module is eligible unless deny covers it. __future__ is never eligible, because a lazy future import is invalid.

An entry covers the module itself and every module below it. sqlalchemy covers sqlalchemy and sqlalchemy.orm, but not sqlalchemyx.

When both deny and allow cover a module, the most specific entry wins. With deny = ["sqlalchemy"] and allow = ["sqlalchemy.orm"], sqlalchemy.orm is lazy and sqlalchemy.pool is not. Listing the same entry in both deny and allow is a configuration error, and lazy-fix exits with code 2.

Matching uses the module's fully qualified name. A relative import such as from .action import Action in src/herogold/logic/trigger.py is matched as herogold.logic.action. lazy-fix works out the package by following __init__.py files up from the file. A relative import in a file that is not inside a package is skipped.

from . import x is matched as the package itself, or as package.x when x is a submodule.

items.title: Excluding files
items.text: exclude takes gitignore-style patterns, matched against paths relative to the project root. They apply on top of .gitignore and dot-prefix skipping, and also to files passed on the command line, so they work in pre-commit.

items.title: Invalid values
items.text: A value of the wrong type logs a warning and falls back to the default for that key.

items.title: __lazy_modules__ sync
items.text: On a project that can't use lazy import syntax yet, fix makes the __lazy_modules__ list in each file match the eligible imports exactly. It adds missing entries and removes stale or denied ones, and it deletes the list when no import is eligible. check reports a missing entry, a stale entry, and a marker placed below the imports it governs.

items.title: Python version targeting
items.text: lazy-fix reads requires-python from pyproject.toml to decide whether a file can use real lazy import syntax (3.15+) or needs the __lazy_modules__ fallback instead. See PEP 810 and lazy_modules.

items.title: Install
items.text:
uv add --dev lazy-fix

Requires Python 3.15+ to run.

items.title: Check a repository
items.text:
lazy-fix check .

Recurses from the given path, considers .py files only, and skips dot-prefixed directories/files and anything matched by .gitignore. Reports every eligible import that isn't lazy yet and exits non-zero if it finds any.

items.title: Fix a repository
items.text:
lazy-fix fix .

Rewrites eligible imports in place. Add --diff to preview the changes without writing them:

lazy-fix fix . --diff

items.title: What counts as "eligible"
items.text: Every module-level import is rewritten unless your deny list covers its module. See the configuration reference. lazy-fix never touches from x import *, and only rewrites module-level imports (not ones already inside a function body or conditional block).

items.title: PEP 810 and __lazy_modules__
items.text:
PEP 810, "Explicit Lazy Imports", was accepted by the Python Steering Council on 2025-11-03 and ships in Python 3.15. It adds lazy as a soft keyword in front of an import statement:

lazy import json
lazy from pathlib import Path

The import only actually runs the first time json or Path is used, not at module load time. Unlike the earlier, rejected PEP 690, this is explicit and per-statement rather than implicit and global — you opt in one statement at a time, and only at module level.

items.title: The pre-3.15 fallback: __lazy_modules__
items.text:
PEP 810 also defines a forward-compatibility marker for projects that can't require 3.15 yet:

__lazy_modules__ = ["expensive_module", "expensive_module_2"]
import expensive_module

On interpreters older than 3.15, __lazy_modules__ is inert — the import still runs eagerly. It exists so a codebase can declare which imports are intended to be lazy ahead of a 3.15 upgrade, without breaking on older interpreters in the meantime.

lazy-fix uses this as its own fallback: when a project's requires-python doesn't allow 3.15+, fix inserts or updates a __lazy_modules__ list instead of emitting lazy import syntax, and check verifies that list is present and accurate rather than checking for the syntax itself.

items.title: Pre-commit integration
items.text:
lazy-fix ships two pre-commit hooks. Add this to your project's .pre-commit-config.yaml:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/HEROgold/lazy-fix
    rev: v0.1.0 # replace with the latest tag
    hooks:
      - id: lazy-fix-check

lazy-fix-check fails the commit if it finds non-lazy imports that should be lazy, without changing anything. To have pre-commit fix them automatically instead, use lazy-fix-fix:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/HEROgold/lazy-fix
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: lazy-fix-fix

Both hooks only run against the staged .py files that pre-commit passes them, on top of lazy-fix's own dot-prefix and .gitignore skipping. They accept any number of files, and read configuration from the project root.

items.title: Order the hook before your formatter
items.text:
lazy-fix-fix writes valid but unformatted code. List it before your formatter in .pre-commit-config.yaml, so the formatter cleans up its output in the same run:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/HEROgold/lazy-fix
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: lazy-fix-fix
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.16.0
    hooks:
      - id: ruff-check
        args: [--fix]
      - id: ruff-format

With the hook after the formatter, the formatter has already run, and the next commit shows long __lazy_modules__ lists or import order errors that only a second run fixes.
